lg.evidence: Every name on the glance is imported on it, the data's origin is in its first comment (round 1's fixture.py, the one-joint rack's 252 real recordings); the verbs are update / compute / reset and plain function calls; each output is a dict of numbers keyed 'name (unit)', two small tables (CAN 11 by rung; pass / FAIL per station and rung) or True. 22 lines of code, the contract's 8 steps in order.

fr1.evidence: Each part type is one function returning configured metric objects (name, description, references, unit on every card); PART_TYPES pairs each with its models (IntegratedServo's 14). Caveat: the pairing is a dict in a proposal module, not yet an attribute on the ModelFamily.

fr2.evidence: One update per recording; one rung_table call for runs -> rung; pooled vs per-run stated per metric (across_runs on every card). Station and deployment are thresholds read over the table (judge, highest_rung), not one roll-up call.

fr3.evidence: live == offline exactly (running sums in row order, round 1's per-sample stop tracker), stops safe across chunk boundaries, alignment stated and enforced (unaligned or backwards rows refused). Memory grows with the stop count, and with every row for Lag: not bounded.

fr4.evidence: Threshold(at_most, unit, owner) never enters a metric; owners Zach / agent / proposed on every line of the three gates; the verdict shows the median and the worst stop per rung cell (36 of 36, 33 of 36).

fr5.evidence: A new metric is one constructor call (TrackingError('velocity error RMS', field='velocities', ...) in the session); a new part type is one function returning a MetricDict.

fr6.evidence: Says where each copy goes (robot_msgs.compare the home, sim2real.metrics and robotdx stock call it), but keeps a streaming RMS beside robot_msgs.compare.error_stats, which cannot be fed chunks.

fr7.evidence: StopMetric.view() carries the data-ui hint ('distribution'); one view goes to matplotlib (a PNG), a W&B payload and Rerun calls written to an .rrd.

lg_unexplained: RMS: root mean square, not spelled out on the page (standard in scikit-learn and Keras)
